sources: KINLINK A+B+C doctrine PDF / full spec
authority_rules: Immutable preconception anchors define historical A but can be explicitly superseded for future behavior only with reason/evidence.
Explicit user product feedback is authoritative for desired behavior/preferences, not proof that implementation exists.
FIELD/device receipts outrank simulations for field claims.
Exact-head CI outranks design prose for machine-tested claims.
Derived summaries and retrieval scores are navigation aids, never canonical truth by themselves.
Conflicting authoritative facts become CONFLICT/HOLD until resolved; never silently merge.
retrieval_contract: load B expansion ledger and research corrections
load last checkpoint and next action
context_pack_budget_rule: Prefer a minimal authoritative pack over replaying full history. Cold history remains searchable and reconstructible.

supersession.rule: Never delete an old canonical fact merely because a new one is current.

idempotency: Every durable mutation/communication action must have a stable idempotency key or provider receipt used for reconciliation.
single_writer: Critical mutable scopes use one active writer and revision/fencing semantics. A superseded writer becomes read-only.
readback: An API success without readback is not COMMITTED for critical state.
privacy: Secrets, signing material, tokens and unnecessary raw network identifiers are excluded from public/project memory.
compaction: Indexes/summaries can be rebuilt or replaced; canonical events/evidence are retained according to explicit retention/tombstone rules.
interruption_rule: On interruption or unknown result, reconcile durable state before replaying any action.
communication_rule: Communication and product work are separate state machines; active mission continuation after forced close requires a new START before more substantive work.
